notes:
Summary: Aurora evaluates Redwood Private (VPC) for customer-facing chat + risk-scoring pipelines. Primary security asks centered on audit logging and KMS integration for compliance with financial regulations (MiFID II/GLBA equivalent).

Key audit/logging requirements (customer-provided):
- SIEM export: want push and pull options. Preferred target: Splunk HTTP Event Collector (HEC) or Kafka topic (internal Splunk-forwarder). Also asked about Datadog/Elastic ingestion adapters.
- Transport: TLS 1.2+ mutual TLS for log delivery; signed log batches (HMAC) for tamper detection.
- Schema: Expect structured JSON schema with fields: timestamp (ISO8601), event_type, user_id/actor, request_id, model_id/version, route, latency_ms, token_count_in, token_count_out, src_ip/vpc_endpoint, action (create/update/stream/error), response_status, redaction_flags. Need mapping doc for Splunk sourcetypes and field extractions.
- Access logs: admin console actions, API key lifecycle events, model rollouts, route changes. Need both human-readable and structured audit trails. Must include impersonation/audit context for SSO actions.
- Retention: regulatory request for 7 years for audit events in EU; default 2 years for operational logs. Need configurable per-log-type retention and automated export to customer S3 (EU region) for long-term archive.
- Integrity & non-repudiation: optional signed manifests and sequence numbers to prove completeness when exporting to SIEM/archival store.
- PI/PHI handling: redact prompt contents containing PII before logs forward; provide deterministic redaction hooks (regex + allowlist) and redaction metadata indicators in schema.
- Throughput & durability: batch-forward mode with backpressure; SLA requirement: no data loss on 99.99% of deliveries; buffer sizing and fallback to durable queue (customer-managed S3) discussed.

KMS integration specifics requested:
- Use-cases: envelope encryption for stored logs in S3, key wrapping for archived bundles, signing keys for manifests.
- Required: AWS KMS + HSM-backed keys (CloudHSM) OR customer-managed HSM. Client must be able to rotate keys on a 90-day cadence and revoke keys with re-encryption plan.
- Integration: Redwood Private should support customer-specified KMS ARNs, IAM cross-account roles for key use, and an offline key escrow option for legal hold.

Data residency:
- Primary requirement: logs for EU customers must remain in EU region; no transatlantic replication without explicit consent. Customer expects region-tagged export endpoints and proof of residency in drive/deployment docs.

Notes from calls/quotes:
- "We need a VPC-forwarded, signed audit trail we can ingest into Splunk — anything less will fail our compliance review." — Head of InfoSec
- SE asks: Acceptable log volumes? Aurora estimates 120M events/month at peak across chat and batch embedding pipelines.

Technical constraints / preferences:
- Prefer server-side redaction with hooks to send redaction tokens back into logs rather than full prompt material.
- Need log sampling controls (10% debug full payload, 100% metadata) with sampling label in schema.
- Want a mapping example for Splunk sourcetypes + Kibana ingest pipelines.

Commercial/Procurement notes:
- Procurement timeline: legal + security review through March; procurement to sign by mid-April if logging and KMS approach accepted.
- Competitive pressure: evaluating Anthropic and managed OpenAI private endpoints.

Internal AE/SE notes:
- SE to deliver detailed logging schema doc (action: Marco Ruiz) by 2026-03-12.
- Security team asked for PoC that demonstrates Splunk HEC push + S3 archival with customer KMS. PoC target: 2-week window starting 2026-03-16.
